Definition: permanence; hence (concrete) permanent; specifically a chieftain
BiblicalUsage: ʼêythân is a plain word for permanence, enduring. It appears in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy, and each time it carries that same plain sense. The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: ʼêythân convinces me that strength is not something we muster; it is something God gives to the weak. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
